title: Canonical finite-model coefficient-topology Hom maps
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For maps $a:\Lambda_0\to\Lambda_1$, $b:\Lambda_1\to\Lambda_2$ of commutative condensed ring objects [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $A_i=p_X^*\Lambda_i$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and use internal $A_i$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $L_a= A_1\otimes_{A_0}^{\mathbf L}(-)$, $U_a=\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}$, and $L_a\dashv U_a$ for the specified K-flat scalar adjunction with unit $v\mapsto1\otimes v$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. Use relative derived tensor and internal Hom $H_i$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $\mu_a:L_a(V\otimes^{\mathbf L}W)\simeq L_aV\otimes^{\mathbf L}L_aW$ be the K-flat derived lift of the scalar-unit-normalized ordinary tensor comparison [def-sfb-internal-scalar-tensor-comparison]. Define
$$\phi_a(K,N):L_aH_0(K,N)\longrightarrow H_1(L_aK,L_aN)$$
as the tensor-Hom transpose of $L_aK\otimes^{\mathbf L}L_aH_0(K,N)\xrightarrow{\mu_a^{-1}}L_a(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}H_0(K,N))\xrightarrow{L_a\operatorname{ev}}L_aN$. The Koszul symmetry gives the equivalent convention with the Hom factor first. Let $\alpha_{a,b}:L_b\circ L_a\simeq L_{ba}$, be the canonical left-adjoint comparison to the exact composite restriction, including its adjunction-unit normalization. Define $\chi_{a,b}(K,N):L_bH_1(L_aK,L_aN)\to H_2(L_{ba}K,L_{ba}N)$ by $\phi_b$ followed by contravariant transport through $\alpha^{-1}_{a,b,K}$ and covariant transport through $\alpha_{a,b,N}$. Define the evaluation-route arrow from $L_{ba}H_0(K,N)$ by $\alpha_{a,b,H_0(K,N)}^{-1}$, then $L_b\phi_a$, then $\chi_{a,b}$.

Write $G_i=R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},-)$ after exact forgetting of internal actions [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. The canonical localization composition comparison identifies $G_0U_a\simeq G_1$. For a specified $f:L_aV\to W$, define its restricted adjunct to be $\eta_{a,V};U_a(f)$ and define its globalized arrow $G_0V\to G_1W$ by applying $G_0$ and this coefficient-forgetting identification. Composite restriction uses the canonical exact-functor comparison $U_a\circ U_b\simeq U_{ba}$.

In particular fix a prime $\ell$, the normed algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite intermediate field $E$, the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring $C$ [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and the all-norm-continuous function ring $B$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], with inclusion $c:C\to B$. Put $A=p_X^*C(-,E)$, let $a:C(-,E)\to C$ be the existing inclusion, and set $S_C=L_a$, $S_B=L_{ca}$ and $J=L_c$. For $V\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)$, define $m_V^C:S_CV\to U_cS_BV$ as the restricted adjunct of $\alpha_{a,c,V}$, and define its $A$-linear form by restriction along $a$ and composite-restriction comparison. On K-flat tensors it is $z\otimes v\mapsto c_X(z)\otimes v$. For $K,N$ in that category define $D=H_A(K,N)$, $H_C=H_{C_X}(S_CK,S_CN)$ and $H_B=H_{B_X}(S_BK,S_BN)$. Define $R\Gamma(m_V)$ by globalizing $\alpha_{a,c,V}$, and define the actual induced global Hom arrow $\Psi_{K,N}:G_CH_C\to G_BH_B$ by globalizing $\chi_{a,c}(K,N)$. All these are specified constructions; no flatness, completeness, constructibility, or site-perfectness hypothesis is part of their definition.
